newsitem.title: BELGIUM: WEAK BFR, UPCOMING AUCTION STRETCH OLO/BUND SPREAD.
newsitem.headline: WEAK BFR, UPCOMING AUCTION STRETCH OLO/BUND SPREAD.

text.p: Continued slippage by the Belgian franc due to unresolved political worries and next Monday's OLO auction hurt prices of Belgian government bonds on Wednesday, but dealers said a recovery would not be far away.

The concerns and some pre-auction position juggling caused the 10-year OLO/Bund yield spread to widen to seven basis points at 1630 GMT from five bps late on Tuesday and dealers foresaw levels of eight to nine bps up to the auction.
The current lack of sellers would come to the foreground again after the auction, dealers said. "Then we will go back to three to four (bps) on the spread again," said one.
One analyst said, "An eight basis point spread is a more appropriate level than the recent low of three."

"But a significant further widening is not looked for given the favourable fundamentals: low inflation and long-term rates, positive EMU prospects and improving public finances as evidenced by today's tax receipts news."
Total fiscal receipts were up 0.9 percent in January from January 1996, the Finance Ministry said.
The analyst noted there was unabated strong support from a significant contingent of domestic investors, who hold up to 95 percent of outstanding OLOs.
Dealers said today's slippage -- they refused to call the move a correction -- was also due to a complete lack of any Bundesbank easing expectations.
The German central bank's policy-making council holds a regular meeting Thursday.
The market would also be on the outlook for German M3 data. No release date has been set.

Meanwhile, the franc and the ultra-short end of the market continued to be dogged by concern there might be fresh skeletons in the closet of the French-speaking socialist partner in Belgium's ruling four-party coalition.
The party is at the centre of bribes-for-orders scandals, which have been deepening in recent days.

So far the other coalition partners have been relatively reticent about the alleged corruption, but as the socialists sink in deeper, the government as a whole could become tainted as well and a breakup, and possibly new elections, might result.

While domestic players discard such scenarios, the currency market has nudged the franc down amid a lack of a clear resolution of the situation. One-week repo rates have risen to offset the franc's weakness, but the domestic dominance of the bond market has meant OLOs have not been affected.
